WHERE TO START

You can take this
one step at a time.

1

Ask for guidance.

If a death has just occurred, follow the guidance of the relevant medical professional. A local funeral director can explain the practical next steps.

2

Contact the registrar.

Registration requirements depend on the circumstances. In England, the medical examiner or coroner process may come first. Ask the local registrar what is needed and when.

3

Take your time.

You do not need to decide every detail at once. Think about who you would like alongside you for a first conversation.

A few things to gather, when you feel ready.

HOW WE CAN HELP

Every funeral
is different.

Some families know exactly what they want. Others have never been asked the question. Either is fine.

Burial and cremation

Traditional services at churches, crematoria and cemeteries across Somerset.

Direct cremation

A simple cremation without a service, with ashes returned to the family.

Woodland burial

A natural setting. Availability and local requirements need confirmation.

Celebrations of life

Religious, non-religious or personal services reflecting the person who died.

Planning ahead

Record your wishes for a future conversation. This concept does not sell regulated pre-paid funeral plans.
